code: for (b = j = 0;  j < input_length;  ++j)  if (delim(input[j])) b = j;
note: The input-controlled punycode label is scanned for the last '-' delimiter and the delimiter index is stored in b.
The delimiter position controls how many leading basic code points are copied into the output buffer.

The safety obligation is that decoding must start after the delimiter when the delimiter is present; vulnerable code failed to advance b for a delimiter at index 0, so '-' was decoded as payload rather than skipped.
The adjusted delimiter index determines the first byte consumed by the variable-length integer decoder.
On the vulnerable path the delimiter byte itself is consumed as a punycode digit, producing an invalid decoded output for an empty ACE label.
